text:
Maya (CSM): Heads-up from procurement 30 they need a one-paragraph SLA + one example credit calc they can paste into the contract. Can we send something clear by EOD?
Arjun (Acct Exec): Short + unambiguous. Procurement hates fuzzy language.
Jonah (SRE): I'll draft an operational paragraph. We'll call out measurement window, the exact endpoints included, basic exclusions, and the credit tiers.
Priya (CS Ops): I can prep the evidence bundle (availability CSV, request counts, sample traces). Will also add the PromQL we run.
Maya (CSM): If possible, include the p95/p99 latency SLOs too. Some customers use that to set expectations.
Jonah (SRE): Agreed. Draft below. Use as-is for procurement: they can paste into the service agreement.

```
Service Level Commitment (Hosted Inference API): Redwood Inference guarantees 99.95% monthly availability for the hosted inference API endpoints (api.redwood.ai/v1/generate and api.redwood.ai/v1/stream) measured per UTC calendar month. Availability is calculated as (1 - total_seconds_unavailable / total_seconds_in_month) * 100, excluding scheduled maintenance with >=72 hours notice and outages caused by customer-managed networking or credentials. Performance SLOs for successful non-streaming generation requests are: p95 latency < 300ms, p99 latency < 800ms. In the event of a monthly availability shortfall, customers may receive service credits per month as follows: 99.95% 50% = 10% credit; 99.90% 50% = 25% credit; <99.00% = 50% credit. Service credits are applied only to the monthly invoice covering the affected period and are the sole remedy for SLA breaches.
```

Jonah (SRE): For measurement, recommend adding this PromQL example they can reference in the SOW: 

```
(1 - sum(increase(api_http_request_errors_total[30d])) / sum(increase(api_http_requests_total[30d]))) * 100
```

Priya (CS Ops): I'll generate the sample evidence bundle: availability CSV, per-route request counts, top 10 traces for any incidents in the window, and a short calc sheet that shows how we compute the credit in a worked example.
Maya (CSM): Can you also add a one-line "how to request credits" with the support email + required fields? Procurement likes process steps.
Priya (CS Ops): Yep. I'll include: support@redwood.ai, invoice month, affected timestamps, and the evidence bundle link.
Arjun (Acct Exec): ETA? Procurement call in the morning. If you can post the paragraph + link to the bundle before 5pm PT, I5ll hand it off.
Priya (CS Ops): Uploading to the shared drive by 4:30pm PT. Will post the link here when done.
uptime-bot: Scheduled maintenance notice: 2024-02-12 03:00-04:00 UTC 50 maintenance for non-prod infra 50 not counted as outage per SLA.
Jonah (SRE): Quick edit proposed for legal clarity: replace "are eligible for service credits" with "are entitled to service credits" and change "applied only to the monthly invoice" to "applied to the invoice for the affected month". Small but reduces ambiguity.
Maya (CSM): Good tweak. Use Jonah's wording.
Priya (CS Ops): Link posted: https://redwood.share/folders/sla-evidence/1711122334 (contains CSV, traces, PromQL, and a sample credit calc sheet).
Maya (CSM): Perfect 50 I'll paste the paragraph + link into procurement email now. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Arjun (Acct Exec): Solid. This should keep legal happy and speed the procurement loop.
Jonah (SRE): If procurement asks for raw metrics, point them to the Prometheus export; I can share a read-only dashboard for the month.
Priya (CS Ops): Adding the dashboard link to the bundle.
Maya (CSM): Closing loop. If procurement pushes for different credit tiers, loop us in. Otherwise we'll treat this as final for the SOW.
